body: Nestled atop a hill in Kandy, Sri Lanka, the Bahiravokanda Vihara Buddha Statue is a striking monument that captivates visitors with both its grandeur and serene presence. The statue, which stands at an impressive 80 feet tall, is one of the largest of its kind in the country and offers a commanding view of the surrounding landscape.
reviewer: kandy tuk tuk tours by munasingha
title: we can climb the top of the hill for panoramic views of the City of Kandy

body: The Bahirawakanda Temple is accessible through a flight of stairs. It houses a Buddha statue that reaches a height of 25+ metres, making it one of the tallest statues in Sri Lanka. You can climb to the top of the statue via another flight of stairs.Sightseers end up taking half an hour to reach the Bahirawakanda statue top as they cannot help halting to take in the view along the way. It is scenic and a magnificent sunset spot. The Sun dipping behind the Kandy hills is something you will remember for years.After purchasing the ticket (LKR 300), I climbed up to the Bahirawakanda Temple first. After bowing my head, I roamed around the terrace, taking in the view of Kandy city below.Here, the Bahirawakanda Temple caretaker recommended that I could go upstairs to the top of the statue. Thus, I began the climb. From the top, it was a beautiful sight.I was standing next to the ear of the Buddha statue. Sadly, the day was cloudy; else I would have been in for a gorgeous sunset. A proper deck has been built to ensure at least 10 visitors can stand easily.
title: A Magnificent View from the Top

body: Temple on top of a hill with panoramic views of the city. The climb is steep, so it is better to use a tuk-tuk. The area is not large, however, there are places for solitude and meditation. From the back of the Buddha statue you can climb to the observation deck at the level of his shoulder blades. In the shop, to the left of the Buddha statue, you can buy religious souvenirs, including incense sticks. At 6 pm the monks recite mantras. Entrance 300 rupees. You must take off your shoes at the entrance; to the left of the entrance there is a special room for storing shoes; the cost of storing one pair is 100 rupees.
title: A place for meditation and contemplation

body: For all the temples I visited in Sri Lanka, this was the most peaceful. Bahirawakanda Vihara Buddha Statue, located in Kandy, is a magnificent sight to behold. This towering white statue of Lord Buddha overlooks the city, offering panoramic views for miles. It has a serene atmosphere, peaceful surroundings, tranquility and provides the opportunity for reflection and spiritual contemplationI was blessed by a monk and felt a temporary release from my turmoil. It’s a small climb to reach the statue which can be by foot or Tuktuk.Small entry fee for the upkeep of very well maintained grounds Great for photography. Overall, Bahirawakanda Vihara Buddha Statue is a must-visit attraction for anyone traveling to Kandy, offering a blend of cultural significance, natural beauty, and spiritual tranquility.
title: The best of all Buddhas in Sri Lanka

body: Located up in the mountain, it is a short drive from Kandy’s downtown area. There is an entrance fee here and shoes are required to be taken off. The steps leading to the statue of the Buddha are cemented and are easy to go through. One can climb the Buddha from its back area. Monks are noted doing their activites.I briefly talked to one of them, he speaks English! There is a small area where small statues of Buddha are on display. Note also that due to its location, one can see the downtown areas of Kandy. One can browse and shop at the small Gift Shop. I was surprised to see a man asking for donations from visitors here.

body: This place is couple of miles away from the city center. One can take a tuk tuk and visit this place. You get the best view of Kandy from the top of the statue. To go to the top of the statue, one can climb the stairs behind the statue.

body: Bahirawakanda Vihara Buddha Statue, located in Kandy, Sri Lanka, is a magnificent sight to behold. This towering white statue of Lord Buddha overlooks the city, offering panoramic views and a serene atmosphere. Visitors often praise its peaceful surroundings and the opportunity it provides for reflection and spiritual contemplation. The climb to reach the statue is relatively easy and offers a rewarding experience, especially during sunset when the sky is painted with vibrant colors. Many also appreciate the well-maintained grounds surrounding the statue, making it a perfect spot for photography and enjoying the beauty of nature. Overall, Bahirawakanda Vihara Buddha Statue is a must-visit attraction for anyone traveling to Kandy, offering a blend of cultural significance, natural beauty, and spiritual tranquility.
title: Blend of cultural significance, natural beauty, and spiritual tranquility.

body: Bahirawa Kanda Temple, nestled in Kandy, offers visitors a tranquil escape and unparalleled views of the city. While you can take a tuk-tuk up for around 300 rupees, the descent on foot is a delightful experience, especially during sunset. The towering Buddha statue is a symbol of serenity, and the temple's surroundings provide a peaceful atmosphere for reflection. Don't miss the chance to walk back and enjoy the stunning sunsets, making your visit both spiritually enriching and visually captivating. Highly recommended this place to visit but in the late afternoon around 5pm and not raining days. Please be advised to wear long pants and a top with covered shoulders. The ticket cost is 300 LRK per person.
title: A Spiritual Odyssey.. amazing view

body: Worth the effort of trekking up to this vantage point to get your daily workout!. Navigate past the tourist shop (operated by a youngster, smiling lad who clearly had permission to only switch on fan and lights when potential customers were int eh shop - but not much of interest in the for us), Climb the stairs to the platform behind the statue shoulders for a magnificent vantage point. body: One of few things that you can do in Kandy. I don't say it's not nice, but it's also not a life-changing experience.To enter the place, you need to have knees covered with clothes. If you don't, besides an entrance ticket, you will be also charged with a rented out scarf that you will put around your waist. Also, you will park your shoes before entering the place, since everybody needs to walk barefoot at the temple.The place has beautiful views, but unless you take tuk tuk, prepare that you will walk up some steep hill to get there. And then you will walk quite some stairs to get to the top of the Buddha's statue, using the stairs behind the statue. It wasn't a problem for me, but might be for someone.As at a lot of places, tourists have their own toilets. And to get there at this place, you need to pick up a key at the bookstore, walk a lot to get to the toilets, walk a lot to get back, and then to return the key again at the bookstore. To me, it looked like a lot of hustle to just get to the toilet. Plus I don't understand why do locals and tourists always separated toilets at Sri Lanka.

body: This is a massive White Buddha Statue located on top of the hill at Kandy. By the time we visited this temple, we already had some fatigue visiting too many temples. Therefore, the experience became underwhelming here since we had visited those with comparatively more historical value and intriguing architecture details. As usual, proper attire is required and no shoes are allowed within compound of Temples in Sri Lanka. Few things to note for this temple is the panoramic view from the viewing platforms, some interesting wall painting depicting Buddha’s life and the giant white Buddha statue somehow gave us the peaceful feelings. Nominal entrance fee and donations are encouraged.

body: If you have never been up close to a huge buddha statue, then maybe this is your chance. But we just found the whole experience to be a little bit underwhelming. For starters, you pay to go in. Then inside you are asked for donations. Then when you leave and go to collect your shoes you're asked quite insistently for yet more donations...The view from up there is just 'ok' really when compared to so many beautiful views available in Sri Lanka (and many of them are free)... The views are also obscured quite a bit by ugly power cables and buildings. It's really nothing spectacular.We got excited when we saw some steps behind the buddha which appeared to lead you all the way up to the head. So we ran up them we anticipation, only to be confronted with a locked gate half way up! What an anti climax....All in I would be surprised if you would want to stay any longer than 20 minutes and even that would be a push... Shame. We had high hopes.... Perhaps we've been spoilt by other large buddha statues in other countries? I mean, it is impressive! But you can appreciate it far better from a distance! If you pay to go in there really isn't anything there other than overpriced gift shops and people bagging for donations. Plus you have to crane your neck to look up at the buddha, when it can be seen at a far better angle outside....Our advice would be save your money. Instead go to a restaurant somewhere where you can see the buddha in the distance and appreciate it from there whilst sipping on a nice cold drink that you can spend the cash on instead.....
title: The experience was just a little bit meh...

body: The experiences I had with visiting Buddha statues varied from places to places. The ascent up the mountain at Lantau Island to view the Tian Tan Buddha in Hong Kong was associated with the soothing coldness of the weather at the top.The ardent climb up the famous Buddhist sacred mountain of Mount Emei in Sichuan China conjured up memories of the torrential rain downpour as I struggled up the thousands of wet stairs to view the Po Xian Buddha statue that was mistily enveloped in the cloudy weather at the mountain top. The cold weather was a stark contrast with the humid weather in Kandy. The On the statue itself, I found this white humble Buddha statue in Kandy lacks the extravagant grandeur of her counter part in Fo Guangshan, Kaoshiung (Taiwan) and the meticulous detailed carving of the huge tall Nanhai Guanyin statue in Sanya. It also has no great historical significance or enormity like the 1200 yrs old gigantic stone Buddha in Leshan China. But this white washed Buddha statue illuminates and sparkles at the top of Kandy hill and can be seen from every corner of Kandy. It is like a lighthouse beacon that shines and guides ships in the darkness of the seas. It looms high protecting and guarding the lives of the people of Kandy. I went up the hill to visit the temple early in the morning. The slope up is located opposite the Kandy Police Station at the town center. The weather is cool in the morning and the climb is not physically demanding. I took my time to enjoy the surrounding scenery and the hillside scenery of Kandy is amazingly beautiful as the morning sunlight flooded the town below. No one collected any entrance money for me. I only sought the help of an old man to leave my shoes with him, He did not demand any money from me after I collected my shoes. The compassionate eyes of the Buddha statue looked down at me when I reached the entrance of the temple. It was a comparatively huge seating Buddha statue. I went up to the temple and spent some time walking around the temple compound. Near the altar area, there were photos of few Buddha statues in Sri Lanka and this temple ranked as one with the tallest Buddha statue in Sri Lanka. It was a magnificent Buddha statue and I look like a dwarf when I was standing in front of this looming huge Buddha. From this temple, I ventured around the village of the surrounding neighborhood. The views here were excellent and the environment in that morning was tranquil and serene.
title: Tranquil and serene environment

body: This large Buddha statue is on the outskirts of Kandy, up a hill with a quite steep and winding road leading to it. Other than that though, there's not really that much to see here, apart from a small bookshop and some pictures. Do not expect a traditional 'temple' like in other places, the statue is basically the main attraction here. There is no cafe or anything like that to get refreshments. As other reviewers have mentioned, the whole place is a bit grubby and in need of a good clean up.The entrance fee though is really cheap, it was just over 1 pound sterling, and was not busy or crowded like some more popular tourist places. You can basically look round here in 30 minutes, so its a good place for a quick stop and some photo's.We went there just before dusk, so got to see it lit up at night. body: Bahiravokanda Vihara Buddha Statue is a huge statue of Buddha in Meditation Posture, which overlooks the city of Kandy. The statue has been built in recent years.The statue can be accessed by climbing a steep hill. A Tuk Tuk can be hired from the city for a round trip to the statue. The statue has become a popular tourist attraction and an entry free is charged, which we felt was quite high and unjustified.There are small Buddhist temples and shrines located below the statue. There are stairs behind the statue, which can be alighted to get more cleared view of the city from the top.The statue appears much more attractive, when viewed from the city, especially, when lit up during the evenings.Not a must visit place, except to satiate once curiosity.

This cost around 200 rupees to enter and they also ask for a donation when inside. You also need to give a donation for looking after your shoes. And beware to dress modestly.
title: Beautiful views

body: Beautiful monument, definitely worth a visit. You can see the whole Kandy from it. Most people drive up with tuk-tuk, but I would recommend to go walking - it’s way more fun even though the heat can be a bit disturbing - nothing that a good hat or an umbrella wouldn’t help with. VERY IMPORTANT!MEN AND WOMEN: Bring your scarfs - to cover the shoulders and/or legs. Shorts (no matter how long they are) and showing shoulders is very disrespectful for Buddhists inside a temple. They do not say anything, but it hurt their feelings. Unfortunately today I saw many tourists wearing inappropriately. So, pay attention and be nice enough to respect their tradition. ;)
title: Worth a visit!

body: It’s really big and impressive. But nothing you stay for hours. The entrance price for a bit high. So it’s totally fine to have a look from outside. The view from the mountain is nice. Especially by night. But you better take a tuktuk to get there.
title: Impressive but expensive

body: This temple with the huge Buddha statue is in the city and is easily accessible by Tuk Tuk, the trek up the hillock is also not very tiring.The actual statue is huge and you have steps that take you right up to the top. The view from the top is marvelous and worth the trek. A site not to be missed, in spite of the entrance fee of LKR 500 per person for Indians. This view of the lake is better than from the Kandy view point.
title: Imposing Statue on a Hillock

body: This was adjacent to the hotel we stayed, had a short visit, but lot of steps to climb the elders stayed away. There is an entrance fees and we can climb till the shoulder of the statue to a have great panoramic view of Kandy.At many places, there are donation boxes, but already tickets are purchased should be more than enough.
title: Best Location, Best View, Great Visit

body: Visible from all over the city area, this Buddha status is lit up at night and can be seen from even the opposite side of the lake.A lovely area to have a statue and as most Buddhist temples in Sri Lanka, is a great place to visit.We only visited it from the outside but people inside could walk inside the statue itself which is a nice idea, but not sure how much that adds.Worth a visit even if it's just driving past as it is a lovely statue.
title: Lovely Buddha which overlooks the city

body: Bahiravokanda Vihara Buddha Statue very ancient place in top of the hill.The view is beautiful from the top of the Buddah. very peaceful Place. Highly recommended
title: very ancient place in top of the hill

body: The view is beautiful from the top of the Buddah.Less crowded of tourists, enjoyable to look around and pray and meditate
title: Top of Hill

body: The translation of the mountain name is Demons Mountain. It was where people were taken to be executed. Our driver told us the statue was built to persuade people that the location was ok to visit.There are stairs at the back of the statue to get an even higher view across Kandy. As it is a temple you will need to remove your shoes to visit. You also need to be dressed conservatively or have a wrap around\shawl etc that you can use for the visit.Suggest that you use transport to access as it is up a steep narrow road.
title: Stunning views across Kandy

body: This is a lovely temple on the hills around Kandy. Less crowded of tourists, enjoyable to look around and pray and meditate.
title: Lovely temple off tourists beaten roads

body: We stopped here for what we thought was a quick visit. The view is beautiful from the top of the Buddah. The best part though was our interaction with the monks. We had a chance to meditate and learn about the buddist beliefs from one of the monks. We really enjoyed it!
title: Wow!

body: It’s a must see for every tourist so why they don’t make things a bit more comfortable for us I don’t know...firstly, yes we need to leave shoes behind, but give us a seat so we can remove them.
title: Great view but opportunity for more.

body: Don't do this in the middle of the day! The Budda is not far from town - but the walk is a steep one up the winding road to the top of the mountain. Catch your breath at the base of the statue and then make your way up the steps at the back for the highest viewpoint. The views across Kandy are pretty impressive.
title: Worth the hike

body: Gorgeous at sunset, beautiful views and photo opportunities. It was a good way to spend an hour before dinner.
title: Sunset visit

body: Great temple had a very good time there, the location is amazing it gives you good views of the city of Kandy and it's very peaceful and less crowded than other places .
title: Great temple

body: It is a nice ride with a tuk tuk up there. Entrance fee is 300 rupees per person, and you can leave you shoes for any amount of money you are willing to pay to the old guy at the entrance. View from up there is really nice and relaxing, but I was disappointed that we can climb only halfway up the Buddha, the top was closed. Nice place all in all, nothing much. You must wear long pants and cover your shoulders, it is their holy place. Bring wet wipes to clean your feet after.
title: Nice view and less tourists

body: Has to be explored once you are in Kandy, as you will get a view of the whole city. Not far with a taxi or tuktuk, and doesn't cost anything to enter, unless you want to donate.
title: Best view in Kandy

body: This Buddhist temple in the hill is beautiful. The view of Kandy from the temple also beautiful. You need about an hour here.
title: View

body: If you prefer a less crowded sight and want to enjoy the view, this place is a great (and cheaper) alternative to the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic (Sri Dalada Maligawa).
title: Great alternative to the Temple of the Tooth

body: If you want to have a very nice view of the city and the hills go on the white Budda.The statue la not so nice but you can have a great view
title: Nice Kandy view

body: We very much enjoyed the walk up the hill and the views are quite remarkable. Moreover we were almost alone and could enjoy the quietness of the place.
title: Interesting place and very nice views on the city

body: The place is a little off the track charging an entrance fee. Do visit it if you are around this place.
title: Checkout the view

body: If you have extra time in Kandy, check this statue out. Cost is only Rs 250 to enter and the view from the top is magnificent.
title: Nice views of Kandy

body: Magnificent views of Kandy. This striking white Buddha statue absolutely towers over Kandy and can be seen from pretty much anywhere in the city. It is nicely lit at night which makes it even more prominent after dark.It's a long way up to it! Hire a tuk tuk or you'll be exhausted!
title: Striking Statue

body: A beautiful spot on top of the hill, but not sure whether it’s worth the trek up there if not staying nearby. Entrance fee (200) and they charge to mind your shoes (by donation) which is annoying.
title: If in the area

body: Worth the trek! The Buddha statue is pretty impressive and wasn’t too crowded when we were there! You get to climb up half of it and get to see an amazing view of Kandy! It could be maintained a little better!
title: Nice Buddha

body: Just a waste of time, we hiked to about 1.5 miles but saw a dirty buddhist temple. The buddhist statue is big but that’s all you have. Temple is dirty from inside plus you have to take out Shoes before going inside. All there is no way to wash feet after coming out. Complete miss.
title: Nah don’t do it

body: On a hill just outside town overlookinh Kandy .Nice but small temple but a huge and beautiful buddha that we liked
title: Steep steps

body: The Buddha was pretty cool to see and the view was awesome from up there. It was rs250 each to get in and we are still unsure wether that was a legit entry fee...A warning to everyone, as you do have to take off your shoes I recommend you take them with you or leave them at the bottom of the stairs because when it came to collection of our shoes from the guy in his ‘shoe booth’ he refused to give us our shoes unless we gave him a ‘donation’. Yup, he held our shoes hostage and so I just leaned in and took them off the counter. There is no signs to say there is a fee or a donation for shoe storage so don’t get pulled into that old trick.Also, heads up, google maps doesn’t give you the right location 🙄👌
title: Shoes held hostage

body: You can visit the buddha statue and the temple before or during sunrise. The whole area is opened even that soon in the morning and you dont pay the entrence fee.
title: Sunrise

body: The Buddha statue is overbearing and looks magnificent.But they do not allow us to reach the top of the statue and the stair case maintenace is also not good.They charge a huge sum from foreigners as entry fees but we feel it is not worth that much.There is a trustee by the book stall who keeps harping on donationsIt would have been better is more details of the place and significance was displayed outside for visitors.Anyways since the statute is located at a height, the journey is nice as it gives us a whole view of the Kandy city.
title: Statute is superb but entry fees is steep

body: Lovely views and a nice place but we were not able to get to the top of the Buddha even though we were told we Could? 250 rupees entry and then the man inside said we couldn't go to the top. A bit disappointing.
title: Good

body: The white Buddha statue can be seen from a distance, even from Kandy view point. It seems to be looking over at the city with a protective stance. The drive to this place, especially, the last 7 minutes is extremely precarious so much so that I was almost going to tell the driver to turn back. But once there, it was beautiful and serene, but we didn't find any ladder or steps on which we could climb the statue. This is a chargeable temple, so be prepared.
title: very beautiful and very steep drive...

body: 300R each to enter this great Buddha statue, I mean the statue is incredible but there wasn’t a lot else to look at apart from the statue! It’s worth paying the money just to look at the statue tbh, but be warned, not a lot else to look at while your there! We had a very brief stay of about 30 mins!
title: Great Buddha statue but not a lot else!

body: Monkeys were playing outside when we arrived and we shared the entire complex with only 4 other people. We couldn't get to the absolute top as there was some renovation going on but the view was still lovely. Standing underneath the Buddha's gaze feels like time standing still. There was no entry fee, but a small donation can be given to the guys who mind your shoes.
title: Peace on High

body: From bahiravokanda vihara budda statue, from top you can also over view the kandy town, but you need to remove your shoes to enter the place.
title: Nice and from there you can have panoramic view of Kandy lake

body: Definitely worth a visit and it wasn’t very busy with other people when we went. We walked and it is further than we thought and up a hill so would suggest tuk tuk would be easier. You need to have shoulders etc covered when you visit. You get good views of the city as well fromHere. There is a charge to get in and for them to keep your shoes but I can’t remember how much that was now.
title: Big Buddha!

body: A beautiful statue and yes you can see a Buddha statue in any Buddhist country but it's all part of the experience.
title: Beautiful!

body: Try to visit this place at night time you will get excellent views of kandy!The drive uphill is slightly unnerving so if your scared of heights be careful. You will have to pay to enter - be careful the guy who will look after your shoes will also want a tip don’t be confused by him as the young monk who needs to be paid after!You can walk up to around the statues mid range if you can stomach the small metal stairs but I think it’s worth it!
title: Great if your not scared of heights

body: Entrance-Fee is 250 rupie - also a donation to keep an eye for your shoes is needed. You can walk to the top behind the buddha figure.
title: Nice view and great Statue

body: This is really beutiful place to visit in the evening you have to take a many photos beuty of kandy city there better to go with tuk tuk very very beutiful with lights in kandy city.
title: Amaya Lanka Tours

body: Went to worship the place. For buddhists this is a sacred place and non buddhists it's a breath taking place. Located at the top of the mountain near to the Kandy city. A huge Buddha statue has been built here and people can climb up behind the statue. Has a really good view of the Kandy town. Since this is a Buddhist temple , recommend to wear decent cloths which cover your body. Stay away from bright colours and expect a good behaviour.
title: A blessed place

body: Such an imposing sight, and so inspiring to see, this huge white statue of the Buddha is a must see for any traveller of any religion. The devotion of the Sri Lankans to the Buddha makes a trip to their country almost a pilgrimage and the constant Buddha statues involve the traveller in much deep thought about existence. The beauty of this statue makes it hard to leave and we sat there for some time just gazing at it in wonder. Beauty is a rare thing and there is so much beauty in Sri Lanka.
title: Magnificent White Buddha

body: very calm place, can climb from backside of imposing statue , excellent view from the stairs.smaller temples situated in the ground floor serene and peaceful hill top - every tourist must visit to experience
title: SItuated on the small hill facing the city of Kandy - very attractive statue of meditating Budha

body: We reached Kandy in the evening and our driver took us this to the temple, turned out to be a great decision. They charge LKR 250 per person as entrance fee for foreigners, plus some donations for keeping the shoes. The temple is clean and quiet. One can climb up the stairs to get a clear and amazing view of the city. As it was evening and the sun was just setting, the surroundings and the city looked very beautiful. Would suggest to go in the evening as the floor would not be hot to walk and the weather would be soothing to enjoy oneself and get some nice pics clicked.
title: Amazing View!!

body: the mountain top temple is one place you can have a great view of kandy city. the old city lies like Barcelona.
title: Nice view of kandy

body: Viewing from nearly all point of the city and really nice view to the city from the hight. You can be driven with car or tuk-tuk near the entry point.
title: Impressing Buda statue on the hill near city centre

body: If you want to have perfect view from Kandy... that’s you place!And you get to see the huge Buddha! You can climb up to see it closely!
title: Nice view

body: While driving through town, one can get a glimpse of the Buddha statue located on the hills of Kandy. It is advisable to drive up there, than walk up the steep slope. Entrance Fee: LKR 250. Unfortunately I did not carry a backpack to keep my shoes, so I ended up paying an unnecessary donation of LKR 50, to have my shoes safeguarded. (With all due respect):Avoid visiting, when the weather is very hot. The Temple authorities should arrange, for more floor mats. Socks should be worn, to protect your feet from sunburns. There weren't tourists when we were around, so we had no idea that the end of the stairway was locked - disappointment for sure! Apart from another mini Temple within the main & an amazing view from atop, there isn't much to explore. But one can't deny the fact that the Buddha statue, looks spectacular from a closer view & makes for some lovely photographs.
title: Average yet Breathtaking

body: On the signs there it reads...BahiraWAKANDA, not BahiraVOKANDA as this states but neither here nor there, this is a magnificent view and I love when you are in the city and look up to see it from different angles and then you go there and it is massive and beautiful. The Monk that was on site was kind enough to share why we heard the "explosions" around the city as it was new year and he explained that they were indicators of when it was time to eat, pray, etc on this holy day.If you have limited mobility, be careful, the stairs are a bit steep and please bring your socks. The mats to help safeguard your feet, stop about half way up and feels like you're playing hot potato jumping up the steps. Also, bring your rupees - you need to pay for entry as well as for holding your shoes at the front before you walk up. Also, ladies, make sure you have modest dress. I absolutely loved the view and the serenity and make sure you go upstairs to the small temple up the steps. You have to make this a stop when you visit Kandy.
title: Gorgeous Views - Wear your socks & Bring your Rupees!

body: Very stunning view, very huge, it's worth it to see if you were moving around.nice to also to have some meditation in there with the quietness of the place
title: Stunning view

body: Super impressive up close! Lovely view of Kandy and surrounding region. My wife and I walked up and down, an easy steady walk for those of moderate fitness.Small entrance fee for temple, make sure you take trousers and cover for shoulders. Worth a walk up when in town.
title: Impressive and a lovely city view.

body: We made the trip up to the Bahiravokanda Vihara statue, which is up a very steep track, but it was well worth the visit. You can climb the stairs up the side of the statue, which is about 20 metres tall, but the views over Kandy were well worth it. No disabled access however.
title: Buddhist shrine with great views over Kandy

body: It was evening by the time we got to go up and the sun was just setting, definitely a place to see sun set from. The staff here were really friendly. A lovely place to visit.
title: Amazing view from the top

body: Don’t get me wrong it’s an interesting place; however the main reason for going should be the views of Kandy... they’re pretty damn good. You have to an pay entrance fee in addition to a ‘shoe storage’ fare; I’m not entirely sure that it was worth the money.
title: Go more for the views of Kandy...

body: You cannot go completely to the top of the Buddha, but still you will have a wonderful view of Kandy up there. Make sure to bring some socks, because the floor is gonna be very hot from the sun and shoes are not allowed.
title: Beautiful view of Kandy

body: Impressive buddah and temple. Be sure to visit in the am. You jave to check your shoes before climbing tile stairs to the temple. There's no mats on the stairs & we nearly burned our feet just getting up to the entry. Great view from the temple overlooking the valley.
title: Nice buddah

body: Make sure you climb the hill where this big white Buddha is located and you will be rewarded with a magnificent view over Kandy. You could also take a tuktuk to the top. There is a shack where you can leave your shoes for a small donation just before you enter. You can also climb a set of stairs behind the Buddha for the view. 20 minutes is probably enough time here and it took me about the same to wander up the hill to get there.
title: Dont' miss the view from this huge Buddha

body: Brilliant views and good walk if you’re looking to stretch your legs. Tuk Tuks can take you up and back but it’s well worth the walk up from the main road. Note: wear or pack socks as you will be required to leave your shoes with the shoe minder at the base of the steps and the concrete ground is hot to walk on!
title: Worth the walk up the hill!

body: The temple was not al that special. We only had a few hours so we decided to visit this temple instead of the temple of the tooth. Besides the size of this temple and that there is no admissions fee there is nothing realy special about it.. We did however have an amazing view of the Kandy lake from the temple!
title: First visit in Sri Lanka

body: The Buddha is seen from all areas of Kandy so it was great to see it up close. A steep yet rewarding walk when you reach the top with great views of Kandy. Worth a visit.
title: Impressive with great views of Kandy

body: We got a tut tut up to the Buddha I wasn't as impressed as with the thailands big Buddha so much bigger and more to see wasn't much to see once you claimed the few steps
title: Ok

body: Temple is nice, the statue impressed me.I'm just disappointed (not only here) because place which normally is for free, foreigners have to pay. There is no official price list, even no information about that, maybe it's why local people who I met on the top where surprised that someone charged me there, Price is not that big (in 2018 - 250rupees), but after some adventures in Nuwera Elliya and Ella I have mixed feeling about charging foreigners for everything what is possible :)I'm also not sure that it is worth this price. Statue you can see from outside, and view from the top is not breathtaking :)
title: Are you tourist? Pay!

body: Nothing special. It’s a big Buddha. I’ve seen bigger and better ones. It’s worth a stop by I guess but wouldn’t go out of the way for it
title: It’s a big Buddha...

body: You can be in and out in half an hour. Nothing overly exceptional, but a great photo opportunity if you have some time to spare in Kandy. It is super high in the hills, so definitely recommend getting a tuktuk up there. We were watching some tourists walking up in the 32c heat and it must have been awful, not to mention anti-climactic once you realise there isn't much to see up there.Make sure you have your knees and shoulders covered. Leave your shoes at the entrance for a small fee, or pop them in your backpack. We went at 10am and the floor/steps were piping hot everywhere, it was hard to get some relief. You can climb the Buddha for views over Kandy, but they are somewhat obstructed and when we were there it was very crowded.
title: Great photo opportunity

body: We were so excited that we could climb to the top of the iconic white Buddha. After paying a small entrance fee we started climbing the stairs only to find out that the last few flights were closed. Very disappointing. It would be nice if someone told us.
title: Buddha tease

body: The 88 foot high Buddha atop this temple can be seen from almost anywhere around Kandy Lake. At night it is lit up and dominates the night light panorama. The walk up to the temple is quite steep in parts, but has frequent levelled out areas to allow a quick rest if you get a bit puffed. I stopped twice for a breather and still made it from the girls school to the top in ten minutes. Do the walk early in the morning or late in the afternoon for a cooler climb, but balance that morning mist may take some time to clear to allow clear views of the valley, vs dark road once sun sets. You can of course take a tuk tuk but where’s the challenge in that?There is a small temple that is fairly plain, and a small souvenir shop. There is also a set of stairs behind the Buddha that you can climb to get a higher view. There are toilets for “foreigners” near the souvenir shop. I quite liked the monk statue down in the grotto whose eyes seem to be watching you warily - see my pic. It costs 250 LKR to enter and a donation of 200-500 LKR is expected .
title: Beautiful Buddha

body: Highest point in the city . Offers a good view of the city . Nothing very spectacular but worth a visit if in Kandy
title: A nice huge budha

body: Best time to be there is either early morning or late in the evening. Quite a walk from the city passing the police station.
title: Fascinating view of the city.

body: Worth a quick visit for the views. Impressive size of a large budda. Not much else there. You will spend about 5-10 minutes tips here.
title: Huge Budda. Excellent views

body: On top of the hill you should have seen visiting Kandy. Our driver took a very nice road where normally no tourist do come. On the board of a very nice lake.
title: Very impressive

body: This was a great stop, amazing Buddha statue, absolutely huge. Great views overlooking kandy. Small gift shop at the top. there is a staircase on the back, you can walk part way up. Washrooms also inside the facility. Snacks and drinks available before you enter.it is a steep hill up, i would suggest getting a Tul Tuk to take you to the entrance. To enter you need to remove your footwear and make sure you have long pants on and women also need to cover their shoulders.
title: amazing

body: We travelled here by 3-wheeler. Beautiful views as far as Knuckles and to the city below of course. A staircase takes you to the level of the shoulder and there is a Shrine with images inside as well as a Buddhist shop just outside. Gents no shorts, and ladies remember to cover your shoulders.
title: Beautiful 88 foot tall hilltop Buddha Rupa with good views.

body: There is a steep hill on the way up to the Buddha. When you get to the top, make sure you have a bag to put your shoes in or you’ll have to pay a donation to keep them with a bloke at the door.Costs 250 each for foreigners I believe (baffling law you see everywhere).Not much to read or see up there, a lot of donation boxes though.Views of Kandy are nice and the Buddha is cool. How often do you see a giant Buddha ?
title: Good view

body: Important thing to note if you are planning to go visit this place (or any temple in Sri Lanka) is that you need to were long pants if you are an adult male. Also, no shoes, so you'll have to pay the counter at the bottom to take care of your shoes for your, or if you came with a driver, you can leave them in the car.The road was really narrow so it was really interesting when the drivers need to maneuver around each other. I'm still amazed how good the drivers here are! :DThe statue of Buddha was beautiful, especially on a clear day. However, please do note that you are not allowed to take a picture with it with your back facing the statue as a sign of respect. My guide advised if you do want to take a photo with you in the shot, do one of those "looking over the shoulder back at the camera" shots.Climb up the statue to be treated to a great view of Kandy. You will be able to see the lake and also other landmarks like the old jail from here.Be sure to leave a donation before your leave. The counter is right in front of the stairs going up the statue.
title: Beautiful statue, great view

body: The Buddha is an imposing sight over the city of Kandy and no less impressive close up. It’s a 15 minute tuk tuk ride to the top, only 500 rupees to get in but then another donation is more or less demanded by a man in a little cabin as you get inside, which was a bit weird as they may as well just charge you once. Still, worth a look as it also offers great views over the city.
title: Lovely statue, great views.

body: We got a Tuk Tuk up here from Kandy Lake. It’s pretty cool but I’m not sure it’s worth the journey up the hill. It’s a beautiful monument but if you’re looking for a good photo it’s going to be difficult as the space around the Buddha is very limited, meaning a well framed shot is nigh on impossible. I’d say only visit if you’re very near by. On the plus side - the view from the top is great!
title: It’s ok!

body: The hike up from the center of town isn't too bad in the late afternoon when most of the route is in shade. They expect a donation to 'watch' your footwear. Then another 250r for the entry fee. The staircase behind the Buddha was gated/locked about 3/4 of the way up when i visited, which was disappointing. Even so, the views along the way were great. Round trip (including walking up hill) i spent about an hour total.
title: Great views

body: A beautiful Buddha Statue, one of the largest statues in Sri Lanka and the highest in Kandy. A steep hillside terrain approximately 2km from the city centre. You can take a tuk-tuk or walk up the steep winding slopes up to the top. Please take your shoes/footwear off at the entrance. A few of 500Rs. Or more for admission from memory. The views from the top of the Buddha are very nice. Don’t forget your camera!
title: Beautiful view of Kandy

body: We wanted something quick to do after breakfast and so used a tuk tuk to drive us up to the Buddha, wait for us there and then take us into the town centre. It was a lovely chilled way to start the day. The views were amazing and the small shop had some great bits which were cheaper then in other gift shops. We stayed at the Buddha for about 30minutes in total. The views from the Buddha and the drive were great. I'm not sure I'd walk it as it is quite far and obviously get hot. A tuk tuk drive was perfect.
title: Quick Buddha visit.

body: I love this big Buddha and the view on him. you can climb up on his back and see a great view on the envoirement of kandy
title: Great View and important place for Buddhism

body: I must admit we were slightly over temples and statues but decided to do this one .Modest entree fee and tip for holding your shoes.Fantastic view over Kandy city,lake and backdoor view into the prison in town.Worth the view but watch out for hot feet on the stairs up.Very hot
title: Another Buddah statue but amazing views over Kandy

body: Cheaper than many things to do in the area, great views from the top, you can climb the buddha and a sari is provided for free
title: Cheap and great views

body: We took a tuk tuk to the peak where this site is located. You could walk, but if it hot, that might not be so comfortable! I saw that some people did walk, but they looked hot! The tuk tuks are cheap.It has a stunning panoramic view of Kandy, especially out to the famous international cricket ground. You simply walk up a couple of fairly easy staircases and you can be behind the Buddha, looking out over Kandy.Worth a visit
title: Stunning views, and quiet too.

body: not crowded. beautiful view from the top. I enjoyed visiting the temple. make sure to wear a shirt and not a tanktop if you are a guy. worth the visit.
title: I loved it

body: I liked here better than Kandy View Point. The buddha statue oversighting the entire Kandy city was amazing.
title: Nice view

body: Good views from Buddha's shoulder. But beware of the shoe "minder". Very aggressive in trying to extract money from visitors. Even to the extent of taking shoes (left legitimately) around the entrance area and putting them in his shack. Suggest you leave your shoes where he cannot see them or simply walk into his shed and take them back. He has no authority to touch your shoes.
title: Beware of the shoe guy

body: This Buddha is placed on the top.of the mountain . Well maintained painted all the time. The Sri Lankan fast on the 1st of January. No alcohol is served at the hotel. This is fantastic.
title: Dec holiday

body: Another must visit, not only to see the impressive Buddha , but also impressive views of kandy city!
title: Great views!

body: Must admit that it is a stunning monument however it is a bit more impressive from central Kandy.....
title: Better from the bottom

body: 250rp to get in. It's ok.... didn't even bother going all the way up... there are probably better places to visit but the view is spectacular.
title: Ok for quick visit. Nothing special

body: The buddha is visible for almost anywhere in Kandy. This place has a entry fees so go here only if you want to pray. You can get a good view of the statue from outside itself.
title: Majestic Buddha

body: Quite interesting to see if you have the time though I wouldn’t necessarily say it’s a must. Don’t forget to make sure shoulders are covered.
title: If you’ve time ...

body: It’s up on a hill and one of the biggest in Sri Lanka so it’s visible from all over town. It’s an easy walk up the hill though, so worth visiting for a close-up look and for views over the town and mountains (the angle of the view is probably not as good as the “viewpoint” on the other side of the lake). You can go up the back of the buddha for a slightly better view (the very top was closed at 10am, maybe it’s never open) and to go inside the buddha, where there are some great wall reliefs. There are also some gaudy offering areas where you can leave a soft drink if you want, so all in all a lot of fun. 250 entry, a bit for the shoekeeper (note they were slack on other clothes, I saw people in shorts and hats) and the monks might harass you for a donation in return for a blessing.
title: Grand white buddha watching over Kandy

body: Well worth the walk up the hill. You can carry your shoes with you if you don't want to pay to leave them in the little hut. Great views too.
title: Super views from the top

body: We visited at 9am and it was fairly quiet. We took a tuktuk rather than walking up the hill. Entrance for tourists was more than for locals and you are asked to give donations when leaving you shoes at the bottom and throughout the temples. Friendly staff and monks. Great views of Kandy and surrounding area. The Buddha statue is impressive and was built in 1988. Worth a visit but not as colourful and interesting as some other temples we have visited whilst in Sri Lanka.
title: Great views

body: Make sure when climbing the Buddha you do it before 4pm, as they close the stair gate that leads you up the final flight of stairs and behind the buddah's head... For some reason?!! And still charge you the same, naturally. We didn't know this, so could only make it up to his shoulders. A nice view, but we left disappointed as we'd done our research and didn't see that information anywhere.
title: Nice view, but time it well!!!

body: My visit here and it was completely worth the hike up the mountain. Well, it’s a long walk up and it can get hot so take water and comfortable shoes. Cover legs and elbows.
title: Tranquility at its fibrst

body: It’s a long and sometimes steep road up to the big white Buddha that you can see from nearly everywhere in the city. To be honest: The statue may be impressive in size but it looks better from far away. You can enter the platform and also go upstairs on the back side of the Buddha, but you have to pay an entrance fee. The view is nice but the view from the Kandy View Point south of the lake is much better and it’s free of charge there.
title: It looks better from far away

body: We took a tuk tuk up and walked back down. Definitely worth making the effort... Great views from up high over Kandy. The Buddha is larger up close and worth this close up view.
title: A must see place for the cultural interest and views.

body: This huge statue of the Buddha is located high on a hill-top and can be enjoyed from a distance from which one can appreciate the size and scale of it. If you care to visit it, a three-wheeler driver will take you and you need to pay a modest entrance fee. Unfortunately it is almost impossible to see the statue or take photographs at close quarters as it is so large. There is a stairway to climb and information about Buddhism available.
title: Can be enjoyed from a distance

body: Tuk-tuk driver took me to this place while on the way to Nuwara Eliya. It dominate the town. The temple and the statue are pretty interesting to see.
title: Nice place on the way to Nuwara

body: Buddha on hill is just about worth visiting as the entrance fee is low You get to go close up to the Buddha statue about 88 feet tall but it’s not that special as the view from a distance is just as good . You need to lean back a bit with neck back to see closely . But it’s only 250 rs to walk around There is a shop to visit and some stairs to climb . Donations are requested .
title: Buddha Statue

body: Located on a hill top, this temple is worth visiting as Kandy is also visible from here-bidr's ey view. A little bit of Buddha's history is available here. Make sure you mention SAARC passport holder to the ticket collector to get discount.
title: Worth Visiting

body: This statue is fine to be viewed from afar!We spent about 5 minutes there. It was only LKR 200 to get in but you also had to make a donation to leave your shoes.Once you’re there it’s difficult to see the statue as it is so large and you are so close and there is nothing else there and no helpful or historical information.There is a nice view over the city, but you can get this from any of the hills around Kandy. I wouldn’t recommend going, instead look and enjoy the statue from afar.
title: Don’t need to visit to wnjou

body: The road to this Buddha statue is more one to do by tuktuk: good, but narrow and steep. Entry fee is 350 rupees. the statue itself does not provide much of an history; it is all about the vieuw. You can climb up the stairs to get the best pictures.
title: Beautiful shaped buddha, wit stunning view all over Kandy

body: Very good location build this temple, please very cram and peaceful, This is nice viw point in Kandy,
title: Nice Kandy viw

body: This is a Buddhist temple located just outside of Kandy town. From the city centre it takes about 10mins to get there in a vehicle. It has a stunning view of Kandy town including the lake, the railway station, the Dalada Maligawa (Temple of the Tooth), & the former prison.The Buddha statue is built in such a way that you can walk inside the statue & see some paintings from the Kandyan era portraying some of Lord Buddha's stories. You can also climb to the platform on the top, so that you get a better view of the town.For Buddhists it's a place of worship, but for tourists, it's also an attraction, because of the view from there. However, I feel the local authorities are misusing it. As a local, I have been visiting this temple for many years, but now it's become more a business than a religious place for praying.Tourists please be aware:You have to pay an entrance fee, but it's not a must to donate cash to the temple. Some of the people there are adamant, but don't feel forced to donate, unless you genuinely want to. Or you can buy something from the shop inside.For locals it's free entrance so you can pray & also enjoy the view. For tourists however, I feel it's not a must in Kandy.
title: Stunning view of Kandy from a vantage point

body: Go in the morning. Any other time might be too hot to too crowded. It's a beautiful viewpoint and quite serene.
title: Beautiful

body: Impressive statue. Built with great effort and finesse that seems to have been lost these days. They aimed for perfection and got it right. Toilets were clean for a change.Use them hereWe walked up and down the hill. Good workout for the morning.Tuk Tuk is another way up and down.
title: Top of the city view

body: This temple is situated high up in Kandy & has a lovely view over the city. It is worth the trip to view, although you are asked for a donation to leave your shoes at the bottom, must pay an entry fee & are again asked for a donation once you reach the temple.
title: Big Buddha

body: great to escape the chaos of the town centre. spent about 1/2-1 hour here. Climbed the steps at the back of the state. Great views of kandy and surrounding hills. Quiet and good to view as the sunsets behind the buddha. Steep walk up and down but can get a tuk tuk
title: peaceful escape

body: On the evening when we went to see the Kandy View Point, this was a temple with a very big Buddha which could be seen even from a distance in the darkness.A brilliant and peaceful place in one of the hills. One can climb up to almost the topmost part of the this Big Buddha structure. This place offers a great view into the city of Kandy.
title: Big Buddha at Kandy!

body: It is good view point and one would usually spend 15-30 min max there, quiet place and obviously for a Buddhist it is good place to come
title: Nice place

body: The Buddhist statue is grand looking and let u overview the Kandy city. For the sake of respect, we have to keep our shoes outside temple. However, when we pick up, staff hold our shoes until donation is given, somewhat not very nice way.We don't mind to donate but hate this way, which is no different from blackmailing. Expect improvement soon.
title: Unfriendly way to ask for Donation

body: We hired a cab to this place using pick me app which was useful. It's a peaceful place, wasn't very crowded when v visited. Has a big Buddha and great view to Kandy city. There is a coconut shop near the entrance, the king coconut water in Sri Lanka is delicious. Do try. The entry fees is nominal.
title: Peaceful place

body: This Buddha statue can be viewed from afar from any point in Kandy! It costs about 150 SLR per ticket to enter, but it is worth it because of the spectacular view of Kandy. You can climb almost all the way to the top of the Buddha statue to see the city below!
title: Fun!

body: This temple is up on a hill. It’s majestically seated at the entrance welcoming visitors and worshippers. You could climb to the top for a great view of the area.
title: A Majestic Buddha!

body: This temple is high above sea level. This temple is a must visit in Kandy. The view from the temple is absolutely stunning.
title: Stunning

body: It is worth a visit when you are in Kandy. Its a walking distance from the town (about 20 min walk up in the hill) or 5/7 min by tuk tuk. You need to pay a tourist entrance fee (about 250 rupies) but the view from the top is breathtaking.
title: Big buddha

body: the bahirawa kanda buddha statue can been seen in the skyline pretty much everywhere in kandy. you can walk up the statute and get great views of the city and the lake too. make sure to wear clothes that cover your knees and shoulders. pretty sure we were overcharged and paid 250rs when I've read others have paid 200rs.
title: beautiful statue and views over kandy

body: It is sacred place like Dalada Maligawa.You can see whole Kandy city when you are reaching there.Windy place.Amazing.
title: Temple

body: Great view of the city, the Buddha itself was very impressive and looks nice lit up over Kandy at night.
title: Nice view

body: You can reach this place by car. The monument is really impressive and you get a nice view over the city. It’s not as crowded as the temple down in the city.
title: Beautiful view over the city

body: My itinerary had no inclusion of this but I asked my driver to take me there when I was at Kandy View Point. It's a peaceful place and a statue itself is beautiful. However, there is an entrance fee of LKR. 250. There is a narrow road leading to this destination. So only small cars and Vans can go here. Not much crowded place. But yes, there are few steps to climb.
title: Amazing and Peaceful

body: i was walking from my hostel going to this beautiful attraction here in one of the mountain in Kandy. And it is really worth the climb while getting here you could notice along the road the huge statue of the Buddha. You get to pay the entrance fee once you come in, but what disappoint me is that you need to pay also the moment you left your shoes in the counter since you are not allowed to get inside the temple wearing shoes. You will be amazed of how big the Buddha is, you can use the stairs at the back of the statue so you could have a beautiful picture of kandy lake and the city. Everything inside the temple is fascinating with different statue of Buddha and its rich history on the pictures of the wall and the ceiling. My experience here is worthy to be treasured.
title: worth climbing for

body: Do you want to view of all of Kandy from one vantage point? Visit the Bahiravokanda Vihara Buddha Statue. You can climb up to about halfway up the statue with lookout points along the way. The walking patio (?) around the base of the statue also has good views, in case you're afraid of heights.
title: A Must Do!

body: Like most Buddhist Temples, this Temple too is situated on a hill top. You have to remove your footwear at the base of the temple (there is a small shanty with an attendant who will keep your footwear for a small tip). Then you climb about 10 steep steps to the 1st level and book your ticket (LKR 250 per head). I was surprised with a Temple charging an entrance fee. I guess they use it for the upkeep of the Temple; but I don’t buy into that logic. You climb another 10-15 steps and get to the main level. The view of the city is beautiful. The Buddhist Temple has a tiny Krishna Temple to its left. According to 1 legend, this was because the Sri Lankan kings used to marry Indian princesses and when the kings used to worship in the Temples, their brides used to stay outside. So the kings and monks agreed to build a little Hindu Temple for the wives to worship and everyone lived happily ever after!
title: Calm & Relaxing Temple (but Entry Fee?)

body: Its a must see attraction, huge Buddha statue beautifully carved very peaceful. The place has positive vibes . Its very calm and peacefully.
title: Beautiful Structure of Bahiravokanda Vihara Buddha Statue

body: I love all the large sitting and walking Buddha's around Sri Lanka. This one has a great view over parts of Kandy. You can walk in from the town or take a cheap tuk tuk. Worth the visit!
title: Great view!

body: Very special place with amazing view and very huge Buddha. Up a hill you can even go walking . It actually feels good to go up walking as if it was a pelgrimage
title: The top of the world

body: First of all I'd highly recommend taking a tuk tuk to visit this giant Buddha as the hill is very steep. Once there though you get a good view onto the city and who doesn't love a giant buddha
title: Good view of the city

body: Can catch tuk tuk up but I opted to walk, a moderate hike as all up hill. Not many tourist so was nice to stroll around and enjoy the peace. Some great views of Kandy and beyond
title: Peaceful and some great views

body: The 88-ft stature at the top of a hill that gazes upon the city is an infatuating sight. There are steps up to near the top of the statue and one can peer down upon the whole city. It is an unbelievable view and the scale of the statue is both beautiful and terrifying.
title: Any Sri Lanka trip is incomplete without visiting this.

body: Impressive in size and beauty. The statue has a calming effect. Perched on top of a steep mountain, you need to be fit to walk up. Still, its worth the climb.
title: Can't help but admire this statue.

body: A proper attraction that must be visited whilst in Kandy. Entry fees are applicable here, just like the rest of SL, and they loot tourists on this as usual. Not very fancy, but not worth the entry fees.
title: Good statue, needs to be visited during prayers

body: Get a lift up here, as the hill is pretty steep and the tuk tuks are cheap, but worth it for the wonderful view.
title: Great view

body: Our reward of spending some of our time in Big Buddha was the panoramic view of Kandy city. Prepare 250 rupees entrance fee and a little tip to watch your shoes. There's nothing more interesting here aside from the huge White Buddha statue and of course discovering Kandy city at the mountain top. Please note that you'll need to take off your shoes/footwear before the entrance gate, so going there when the sun is shining bright is really not recommended.
title: Nice Panoramic view of Kandy City

body: We walked from the other side of the lake up to the Buddha and although a lot of people get tuk tuks, if you enjoy walking I would definitely recommend it as it makes up part of the experience too, otherwise you'll probably be in and out within 10 minutes and I can imagine it would feel like a wasted journey perhaps? It's a lovely place and being able to walk up to the shoulder of the Buddha is an added bonus due to the amazing view you get. It's 250 LKR to get in but bare in mind also that you'll be expected to give a donation in exchange for getting your shoes back at the end..
title: Beautiful view

body: I had hired a tuk tuk driver for the day( make sure you haggle and tell them where you want to go, otherwise they take you places where they get commissions).. its a long ride up the hill.Take your shoes off before you enter otherwise they will charge you for 'minding them '. also small fee on entering. I was disappointed on how dirty and shabby it was, it was in need of maintenance, however another man sat behind a desk asked me for a donation, when I asked what for he said for the temple, I kindly reminded him that I had paid to enter .There are lots of steps leading up to near the top of the buddha and the views are amazing, great photo location, other than that it isnt anything special.
title: Great views of Kandy

body: There is a lot of statues of Buddha in Sri Lanka. This one is not spectacular during day - probably Golden Buddha in Dumballa would be better, but during night all changes 180 degrees. Illumination and the view is amazing. Looks like there is also no ticket just donation if you want to. Take a tuktuk/riksha both ways as you will not find any at the hill.
title: Illumination helps

body: Very huge statue. the place give you a panromic viwe of the city must visit . Use a tukvtuk to visit this hill.
title: On the top of the hills

body: A carm and a quite place in Kandy town. Situated in a mountain top. Tourist destination. Good for meditation.
title: Good place to visit

body: Nice to Go there, Only to Enjoy the view over Kandy city. You can climb the Buddha en see inside. Only 25 years old so no historical value.
title: Only for the view

body: Nothing great. A big Buddha statue. You can see many like these in India. Nothing much there apart from that.
title: Big Statue that's all

body: Was ok, went as part of a four / five place Tuk Tuk tour - just another tick box location in my opinion
title: A quick stop

body: It's situated on a small hill and at night it looks magical with Buddha watching over the whole city.There is a fee that you need to pay to enter the complex of course as is the case with all Lankan temple businesses.People do ask for tips and donations but if this is the second or third day in Lanka then you would get used to ignoring the request. Nonetheless it's calm and serene and a good view of the city.
title: Serene

body: The big Buddha as it is popularly called is magnificent. It can be spotted from the Kandy view point and from many other places as well. The statue is lit up at night and looks just beautiful. I wouldn't recommend taking the (slippery and smelly when it rains) steps all the way to the top as the top most floor was locked which made the climb a waste.
title: Must see - for the sheer size of the statue.

body: we firs wanted to skip this side but then decided to go since the entrance was 250 rupees only, The view over Kandy and sourrounding mountains from here is amazing! :) we loved it and we even got o withes a small pooja ceremony
title: The View

body: One of the must do's in Kandy city, 10 minutes Tuk Tuk ride from downtown, you can climb up, great views of the lake.
title: Good view of the city

body: The view if the Buddha is great. And the view if the city Kandy is spectacular from the Buddha. Entry is 250R and you can climb almost to the top for a great view!
title: Views!

body: Best view in Kandy, as you can climb up the Statue. Beautiful Temple on the inside. Entryfee 200 Rs for 2 persons.
title: yes, worth a visit!

body: Take a tuk up there which will cost you around 200 one way, it's a steep climb so braise yourself. the temple itself is small, i suggest you visit this temple around 6 pm as you still do has some semblance of sunlight to soak in the view of Kandy with great detail and also observe it at night.
title: Bird's eye view of Kandy.

body: Fabulous view to Kandy city center, you can get there by car. If you want to you can donate some rupees in the office for donation.
title: Must visit

body: If you're in Kandy this is definitely worth a visit. Serene and tranquil like all the temples. The view is fantastic from the top as you can climb buddha itself up the steps. Entry 250 rupees each. Leave your shoes at the entrance. Ladies will need to cover shoulders and legs.
title: A must see.

body: A quick, but impressive stop in Kandy. This tall white Buddha sits at the top of a mountain in Kandy overlooking the city. Appropriate dress code for women is to have their shoulders and knees covered. If you don’t come prepared, they do have sarongs for you to wear. You also need to take your shoes off, so on a hot day bring socks in case the floor is hot. We went here instead of Temple of the Tooth and were very happy with our decision. Way more glory to see here.
title: Impressive Buddha statue

body: Gives a very good view of the city. But if the requirement is to view the city go to Kandy View Point. Nice and peaceful place.
title: Huge Buddha Statue

body: Use a tuk tuk to visit there.On the top of a mountain.Worth visit\A huge Buddha Statue facing Kandy city.From the top it is nice to see the kandy city.anytime.
title: Nice plkace to visit in Kandy.

body: You can't miss this white Buddha once in kandy and from near is even better. It's a nice place to be peacefull etc.
title: a sign in the city

body: Later in the day we visited the 88 foot tall Bahiravokanda Vihara Buddha statue. It is possible to climb up behind the statue for panoramic views of Kandy. It is a short visit, there is no real need to stay too long.
title: Great views from the top

body: Huge Buddha statue, where you can climb upto the shoulder. Gives a good view of Kandy city, much better than the 'View point'. You'll be disappointed if you are expecting Nirvana
title: Panoramic view of Kandy

body: Was worth having a look at the buddha statue. Nothing amazing though. Just something to see if you are in Kandy.
title: It's ok

body: We have to remove our shoes/slippers to visit the temple. It's normal. But at least the temple has to be clean!!!
title: Bring socks with you

body: From Kandy city about 2 km.this temple name is bahirakanda temple.we can go by car.we have to wear long Dress before the entrance temple. Is this same other temple. So very beautiful view and big Buddha statue. They charge 250 rupees from foreign people and free for local people. Very nice temple go and see.
title: Very beautiful view

body: 250 rupees entrance fee but with perservance you can get in for free, steep mountain climbing tuk tuk good option to get there, but we managed to drive a van up just!
title: Great views over kandy including the jail!

body: This is worth the visit, for the statue and the views, but the place is showing its age and not the best for walking around in bear feet. Ticket price is 250 rupees PP £1.25/$1.60.It is slightly off the beaten track, so not 100's of visitors. You can drive right up to the building or it is about a 30 minute walk up the hill. You will only need 20/30 minutes at most.
title: A good place to visit with views over the city

body: If you have time it is nice to visit,ticket is 250 rp.The statue is really big and nice.The view is ok but we have seen better.
title: It is nice to visit

body: We visited as part of a day tour of Kandy.The statue itself is quite impressive, but the temple is pretty dirty and not very pleasant to walk around without any footwear. There was no real explanation of anything within the temple, which was a little disappointing, but there is a great view over Kandy from the back of the statue.This was nice enough for a 15-20 minute visit but I wouldn't expect to spend anymore time than that.
title: Nice view but not much else to see

body: Impressive Buddha on top of a hill surrounding Kandy. Great views from the top and a quaint little book shop in the temple grounds to stroll through.
title: Impressive and great views

body: Beautiful structure, beautiful view but there are no text translating the paintings etc so you end up wandering rather than taking in any understanding.
title: Good but could be better

body: This giant statue is pretty close to the center of town. It is rather boring for a westerner who doesn't know much about Buddhism because most signs are not in English. Also, it is a little dirty.
title: Not to exciting

body: The view from this huge Buddha is impressive. There is nothing else to it except for the size - which is better viewed from afar. It's a long drive to the top of the hill also so you will need a car or driver
title: Good view

body: The Buddha is a 15 minute tuk tuk ride out of Kandy centre. It's nice to visit a temple away from all of the crowds. You can climb up the staircase to shoulder level of the sitting Buddha. A pleasant enough trip if you have quite a few days to spend in Kandy. Not really worth the trip up there if you have any time restraints.
title: Peaceful spot

body: Not to much to brag about really. And a bit weird with the steps and platform on the back of the Buddha. At the same time a beautful place at sunset because of the view.
title: Go at sunset

body: It is a trap to tourists. Nothing to see but a man-made Buddha. Hard to walk to there, need to take a Tutu and be careful about those Tutu Drivers. They can ask for 800 LKR just to go to the place though it could cost around 200 LKR. I only took 10 mins to finish all visiting. Highly not recommend.
title: Highly Not recommended

body: It is a hill climb to the top. I visited in a draught period. The toilets were without water making a visitor unable to use until they climbed down.
title: You could view it from far but also you could go right to the top of this hill in your vehicle!!

body: Well worth visiting this temple. You are able to climb up behind the Buddha Statue where you get great views over Kandy.
title: Great views across Kandy

body: We decided to hike all the way to the top on foot and we were definitely rewarded for our efforts with amazing views and an impressive Buddha statue. Climbing up the actual statue was also really cool and you could see for miles. Definitely recommend!
title: Worth the climb!

body: There is a nice view from this statue although it's not free for foreigners and we were told it was. Then again everything costs something in Sri Lanka if you're labeled a "foreigner"
title: Not free as advertised but a nice view

body: The Buddha is a nice place to visit if you are tired of the hustle and bustle of the streets below. It allows good views over the surrounding valley and a little breathing space from the humdrum of town. I've seen a fair few buddhas before and while the site doesn't stand out it was a welcome change of pace
title: Nice and peaceful

body: "Which way to The big statue of Buddha?" I have been helping for lot of people to find out this place as it is not a place that tourists frequently visit. but I suggest you to visit here if you're an adventurous and cultural lover. This place has a great value of old wall arts and some thrilling stories behind this place. This place is also a kind of a view point as you can see the whole town up in here. If you are looking for a place to meditate for a while this is a very good place for it but keep remember to choose a free day to do so. to get here the easiest way is this. find the Kandy Police Station. ( not hard to find.) and there is a main road goes up right in front of the police station and turn in to that road.few meters ahead you will see an another street goes up on left side. if you are planning to get a tuk tuk ask the driver to go on that way because some of them may take you a long way to get more money. it is not more than 150/= from the police station to the Statue. I prefer you to walk because on the way you will see the culture and beauty of Kandy. but you have to walk quiet long way. as you keep walking you will find a Bodhi - A Bo tree with a small Buddha Statue on left side and in front of the Bodhi You will see a narrow street going up. that is the path and do not take turns go straight along that way. you will find the place.
title: A one of the greatest place to visit...

body: We drove up to the Buddha and walked back down. We are not religious but enjoyed the peaceful temple with its great views out over Kandy and the surrounding area. It cost our family of 4 a 1000 Rupees and a ' donation' to the man that looked after our shoes. We spent an hour around the temple.
title: Worth a visit

body: This is a good view point to get a perspective from Kandy city. Other than that, the temple offers little more. Its impressive budha is an interesting view and climbing through its back makes it a nice opportunity to get unique sightseeings of Kandy. The temple itself, though is not so attractive, there's actually little more to do or see. If it's a nice sunny but not too hot day the walk down to town is a good experience and not too far.Entrance 250 lkr
title: Good views

body: I think the view from this place is best in the afternoon.I climbed up the hill to the statue in the morning to start my day. It was an easy 30-minute climb, or walk up, and I was greeted by the sight of monks at the base of the statue. It's a monastery, I suppose. The entrance is free and I climbed to the top of the statue for a nice view of the city -- only that the sun was rising in the opposite direction so the lighting is not great for pictures. An afternoon visit might be best.
title: A nice climb in the morning

body: Good view over the city, entry 250 Rs. ... locals for free. You can climb on budha from back side. Dirty floor, so your feets will be dirty. Takes your shoes to your bagpack, monks dont clean this place, so dont support them via donations
title: Another budha, but good view over the city

body: We stayed in hotel emerald hills and went for a morning walk and accidentally saw this temple board and started walking. Its a nice place for people who loves history, architecture etc. Entry pass for foregin nationals was 1250 LKR, which i feel a bit high for that place. Else a nice view point, clean and silent area.
title: Nice place for a morning walk

body: a very impressive statue on top of a hill can be seen from miles on a clear day from around the town
title: giant statue

body: The Buddhist temple situated on the highest point in Kandy city. You can see the whole city and a huge temple
title: The Buddhist temple situated on the highest point in Kandy city.

body: The view of Kandy was awesome, Meditated for a few minutes. The view of lake and hills was mesmerizing. The top part of the temple was closed. But, overall very memorable.
title: Excellent View

body: this location is a good view point to view the city, spend the afternoon looking at the area, interesting
title: good view point to view the city

body: We visited at night. We got a tuk tuk for 400 rupees from the city and then back to our hotel after. Buddha is beautiful at night. After paying entrance fee we were pressured to make a donation which we refused. Do not feel like you need to pay. I can recommend this to other tourists but the pressure to pay more money really lets it down.
title: Beautiful at night

body: Our visit left a feeling of a total rip off. After paying entry fee and a fee for shoe storage we were asked, if not forced, for donation, even before we saw the place. The two guards - or whatever they were - were just sitting around and asking for money instead of cleaning the extremely dirty floor. Walking around was disgusting, there were dog and bird excrements spread all over. The view over Kandy is nice, but this was the only positive thing about this place.
title: Disappointing

body: There are good views over Kandy, you will not be here a long time. Dont forget to go up the steps at the rear of the Buddha to the top and explore the rooms inside it. In summary good photo op but you cant spend a long time here.
title: Good views over Kady

body: This was one of my favorite sights in Kandy. We took a tuk-tuk from the center of town up to the entrance. I don't think it's walkable from town. As with any temple, you must take your shoes off before entering. I've seen complaints about that in other reviews, but taking off your shoes is not unique to here. It is a sign of respect and a cultural and religious practice. The statue itself is impressive, and there are stairs behind it that lead to small temples and beautiful views. We probably spent about an hour here, maybe a little less, just walking around and checking out the views.
title: Iconic statue and great view of Kandy

body: One of the best spots in Kandy. We happened to go there by chance. You can see the huge Buddha statue from most parts of the city and we did not have a plan to go. We landed up there on our driver's suggestion and could not thank him enough. This is on top of a hill. From there you will get a beautiful view of the city. The status itself is beyond descriptions by words. You can feel the tranquility and calmness. Please do not forget to climb the stairs to go right near the base of the statue. The stairs are narrow and if it rains, may get slippery - be careful. However, the visit will not be complete without that climb.
title: Do not miss a visit

body: Long walk up on the burning tiles, as your bear feet start to become grilled, the reward is a large statue hurting your eyes in the sun. Half views of Kandy, not really special. Before you walk down you will be asked to make a donation as a foreigner.
title: Big statue without special surroundings

body: Unfortunately it was very hot afternoon when we reached this place. To remove the shoes to go up to the statue was painful. Plan a trip in the evening or when you think it would be comfortable to move and walk without shoes on the marble stairs.
title: Beautiful Statue viewed from all over in Kandy

body: The perfect spot to have a sight on Kandy. The statue is amazing and you must wear a long dress to go in. 250 Rs. Fair.
title: The prefect spot

body: It's a nice temple to visit but our aim in going there was for the views over Kandy. It's very high up and ha great views of the town. It's 250 R entry. Slightly annoying in that once you enter - other staff then ask you for donations for the temple.
title: Nice views over Kandy
