body: Very huge Buddha, you can ask a tuk tuk driver to bring you there, I wouldn't bother pay to go in though, as you can easily look at it from outside
title: Massive Buddha

body: The view is good, but it has got a very bad road and we spent hours in traffic jam. When we arrived, they asked us to take off our shoes while the ground and stairs were teribbly dirty. What´s the point of taking off the shoes if everywhere else is dirtier than people´s feet?
title: Not recommended

body: There's a nice view from this statue. A bit of a climb, and make sure you have got something to protect your feet. We hadn't planned going there and didn't have socks to put on. The floor was scorching (as were our feet, which didn't add to the pleasure of the visit).
title: Nice enough but nothing special

body: Went night on a holiday so temple was closed. However got to look around for less money. Many temples here charge you & donations are needed to maintain them.
title: Great visual at night.

body: The Sri Maha Bodhi Viharaya at Bahirawakanda is a very attractive and hilly place in the Kandy Town. ... The omnipresent Buddha statue seen from everywhere in Kandy city. Take a tuk tuk ride to the Temple, just 1 km away from the Kandy city.
title: beautiful lord buddha statue

body: This is the 2nd largest Buddha in Sri Lanka at 88ft tall. It cost 250rupees to enter and you can climb a staircase to the level of Buddha's shoulder. The views are lovely and the Buddha itself very impressive. Well worth a visit if in Kandy
title: Nice for a short visit

body: Amazing place to visit you can see whole Kandy from this place.It is best to visit evening this place to catch Sun set
title: Beautiful view

body: This was a lovely quiet place to visit for fantastic views over Kandy. It was inexpensive and definitely worth a visit in my opinion. There's not much else there to see but worth it for some tranquility in an otherwise busy city. The views from the top are pretty impressive.
title: Glad I went

body: Lovely place at a highest point in Kandy. The city is beautifully seen from here. As the title mentions it has the second largest Buddha statue in Sri Lanka.
title: Second largest Statue of Lord Buddha in Sri Lanka.

body: This Buddha Statue has a 'secret staircase' behind his body which you are allowed to climb. The view over the city is fantastic.
title: Buddha Statue with a view

body: Entrance cost us 500rupees plus lil extra for shoe money. Once up there it's quite impressive and worth seeing however I wouldn't say it's a must see site. Overall a 3 out of 5.
title: The white Buddha.

body: A massive Buddha, from where you can see the entire city, lake and surrounding area. As is always the case, you need to take your shoes off, but beware! On the steps going up there were some cloth mats, but mostly it was just very hot tiles, so if you have sensitive feet, ladies, bring a pair of cloth slippers! My feet were roasted!
title: Great view point of the city

body: Nice serene place. Even beautiful when you see it at night from the Kandy town.There are Hindu gods also in there.Need to take a vehicle there.Steep rise
title: WHITE BEAUTY

body: It is just a 30 mins walk from the city. You can take a tuk tuk also. The steep is not hard to walk. There are boards leading to the temple. So it should be easy to find. On the way you will find a girls school also.The Budhdha statue's height is 88 feets. It was built in 1993 and is in Samadhi Posture. It is one of the tallest Budhdha Statue's in Sri Lanka. There is a good view from the top of the mountain. If you are a lady you have to dress appropriately covering your legs and shoulders since this is a religious place. Otherwise they will give you cloths to cover yourself.
title: Sacred Budhdha Statue

body: Can see the whole kandy city from the top and the monks are so friendly and explaining the history of the place so well
title: View and the history

body: Loved visiting the statue. Had a little discussion with Monk as well. Nice views of the Kandy city as the placer is at top of the mountain and at high altitude. Great place for taking pictures of the city.
title: Up Close, Big Bhudda

body: I loved visiting this statue. It's a great spot for photos, lovely views over Kandy and the lake. Could walk up but I took a tuktuk
title: Great views!

body: This temple is situated at a high altitude. So at the top of the temple you can have a good view of the Kandy city.
title: Visist there to have a good view of the whole Kandy city. Never miss!!

body: Walked to the buddha statue, which is quite a steep walk. Cost a few hundred rupes to get in. Girls have to cover shoulders and knees. If you haven't done that, they will give you a shawl to wear. There isn't much to see or do at the place, and you don't really get a good view of the buddha statue. You will get a better view of the Buddha from the city, especially at night where it is lit.From my point of view, this is not a must do in Kandy. And if you have limited time, I wouldn't go.
title: Nothing special

body: You have to go there to see a beautiful sunset over Kandy. Of course don't miss the Buddha which is incredible !
title: Amazing view !

body: really we are happy to see aplace loke this in kandy and a place with a nice view and we had a nice time there
title: wonderful view

body: Very Attractive and nice place located at the top of the hills in Kandy. Image of Lord Buddha is worth to see .Attracted tourist place in Kandy and from the top the city view is really awesome :)
title: :Nice Place"

body: History of Bahirawakanda goes back to kandyan kingdom era . There is beautiful folk tale about Bahirawa ( the god in charge of land ) is related with this place . You can reach this place within few minutes of walking or by vehicle from the heart of the city . You can feel the calm and quite environment in this place also as Buddhists are seeking real peace in their life . Buddhists believe controlling their mind give the good results to their life . Nice place . Don't miss it .
title: Beautiful Image of Buddha

body: The temple is okay but not neccessarily worth to pay for. The statue of budda is from outside very good visible. You can walk up or take a tuktuk
title: Nice to see but not neccessary to pay to go in the temple

body: Lovely to go and see the views from the top and nice that you can walk up. Watch out for the man at the front collecting your shoes and asking for money, just leave them in the taxi. Around 250 rupees each to go up to the top. Takes around 10 minutes, and there isn't much to it.
title: Average

body: I was on a tight schedule so I just hopped in a tuktuk to drive up to the statue and take some pics which was great. It's a fun journey in a tuktuk as you drive up some quite steep windy roads. The area outside the entrance to the Buddha is quite messy and unkept which I didn't expect. The Buddha also looks amazing at night from afar as it's all lit up.
title: Beautiful up close and from afar at night!

body: This is a giant Buddha on a mountain so it's really high lol but it's a nice place to visit the views are fantastic even better if you like buddhas
title: It was on the tour

body: even if your not a Buddhist you should visit this place because this is one of the view points of kandy you can see all the city
title: one of highest point of the city

body: As the entrance fee was £7.50 plus extra for storing shoes, only my Father went inside while we all took photos from outside. This is an expensive price for tourists. It should be a lower price but request for donation. The statue was impressive and looked in very good condition and behind a high wall, up a steep hill. My Father spent about 20 minutes walking around and thoroughly enjoyed himself.
title: Impressive Statue up steep hill, expensive admission fee, tranquil location

body: As opposed to the Temple of the Tooth which I found too touristic and crowded, I'm really pleased that we drove up to see this statue, its very impressive. It was also very quiet and peaceful when I visited and there are nice views of Kandy. Be sure to cover shoulders and knees otherwise you may not be able to enter, although you can borrow a shawl from there.
title: Lovely and peaceful

body: Must See place in Sri Lanka. So much History but get the right guide, Don't listen to anyone who calls themselves a guide. Take your time, don't rush this place. Light a lamp, and an incense ...
title: Most Sacred, powerful and spiritual, pleasant. Crowded.

body: For foreigners, they charge LKR.200/- per head.Once you visit the entire visit, a person at the entrance will ask for money again in the name of donation.He was very demanding for the same, But I did not pay him anything and told him donation is something which I need to give by my own will, and not asking for the same compulsorily from someone.
title: Good place, entry ticket 200 LKR

body: Amazing to see and really worth climbing the steps to see it. You must remove your shoes before walk up the steps to it. An interesting shop to browse in at the top a Buddhist monk will accept donations to assist in the upkeep of the statue that overlooks a vast area where local people live.
title: Bhudda

body: One of the several largest outdoor Buddha statues in the world.Marvelous artistry.You really need to sit and contemplate . What kind of love and devotion inspires creations like this?A must visit!
title: Imposing Buddha statue

body: The buddha overlooks Kandy and is very well lit at night. It is quite a climb to get there but well worth it. Auto rickshaw good value. Be aware that the shoe man asks for payment so leave your shoes in the taxi. You can climb up the back of the statue for an amazing view. Well worth a visit.
title: Magnificent

body: After visit of Kandy, on the next day in morning while going to Nuwara Elliya, we have been at Bahiravokanda Vihara Buddha Statue. This is tallest statue of Lord Buddha in Sri Lanka situated on a hillock. They charges 200 Sri Lankan Rupee as entry fee for per person. From here we have a nice Ariel view if Kandy. You have to climb just 25-30 steps from your parking. A nice and must see place of Kandy.
title: TALLEST BUDDHA STATUE OF SRI LANKA

body: There are numerous such statues dotted over South East Asia and they give the impression of protection to the town and can be seen from numerous locations in the town. The visit is nothing special but adds to the atmosphere of the area.
title: A backdrop to Kandy

body: We took a tuk-tuk from town up the steep hill to the white Buddha. You can get a round trip for 500R, they'll wait for you at the top. There were very few tourists around when we visited, which was nice. You can climb up the stairs at the back of the Buddha and get a magnificent view of the surrounding mountains. Well worth a visit!
title: Worth a ride up the hill

body: It is hard to get up there - I suggest driving as far as you can. The statues is huge but not artistically impressive. The view is great!
title: Long climb reat view

body: For 250 rupiahs you can enjoy a view of Kandy from the top of the Buddha: just this is worth the visit. We tried to reach it from downtown but gave up at a certain point: we couldn't not find it on google maps and we must have gone the wrong way. However, it should be feasible if you don't bother 20-30 minutes walking. Otherwise, a tuk tuk will bring you there for probably 300 rupiahs or so (we only did the very last part in tuk tuk, once we realized we were kind of lost).
title: Stunning view

body: So interesting. The building is beautiful, has a special feel.No shoes worn in this place, extremely popular with the locals.The history is incredible with all the ancient pieces.
title: Amazing place!

body: The only good thing here is that you can see the whole kandy city from top of the budha. Before you enter, you have to store your shoes by the man in front of it, next there is always a child that come in the ticket office puts some "budha" clothes on and wants money for entry. What you get is dirty place to walk around, you can see dogs excrements everywhere etc. Would not go there anymore.
title: Do not worth it

body: Stunning to see this Buddah up close, great photos contrasting against the blue sky. If you dont fancy a very steep hill climb, get a tuktuk. Also, you need sarongs to cover legs and arms and there is a stall there charging to store your shoes - just put them in your bag, it isn't necessary to pay.
title: Impressive Statue Close Up

body: Huge buddha looking out over the city. Fabulous views of the city. It's a bit of a trek to reach so probably best to take a tuk tuk. Worth a visit.
title: Impressive statue

body: Walking up was nice and the view over kandy is amazing. Totally worth the sweating!The "inside" of the statue for us was not worth the money (250rps.). Not much information and almost nothing to see, except for a souvenir shop.If you want to take the stairs to the top of the statue, you habe to pay the entrance fee though. I say, walking up the hill is enough for a nice view of the city and see Bahiravokanda up close.
title: Just for the view

body: There is a charge for entering the temple area, 250 each. The views from the top (or as high as you can go) are great and you can see far across Kandy and the surrounding area. Remember to keep some small change for the minders to look after your shoes.
title: Great views

body: We drove past this statue several times as it is on the main road. We never stopped to admire it but took pictures as we drove past
title: Large Statue

body: It was the best local for Sunset in Kandy, I loved it, each level of stairs going to the top give a different perspective of Kandy sometimes revealing mountains and lakes and others aspects of the city.
title: Amazing View, do not miss it

body: The massive statue towers above Kandy and can be seen on top of a hill so a bit of a climb to get close. White in colour it catches the sun to really stand out. Good to photograph at distance.
title: Towering Statue

body: This is a nice stop if you have the time, even if only a few photos. There isn't much literature or signage in the area explaining the history of the Buddha. The views are nice.
title: Worth a visit. Nothing spectacular.

body: Didn't have a chance to visit close to the statue but a had a look from distance. Kandy city covered by all the Buddhism heritage while this statue make a mile stone.
title: Big statue facing the City

body: Walk up the hill is a bit of a challenge. People who would find this difficult can opt to use a tuk tuk. The views over Kandy city and lake are very nice.
title: Beautiful views

body: This is one of the biggest Buddha statues in the country, standing on top of a hill, overlooking the city and the Lake of Kandy. We took a TukTuk to the statue, left our shoes with the caretaker and walked the steps to the first floor. You already notice this imposing big Buddha looking down upon you. At every floor you can can see different things and there is always the beautiful view on the valley with the city of Kandy. We walked the three floors and unfortunatley the last gate was closed that day so we could not get really close to the statue. It was a nice experience.
title: Feeling small next to this big Buddha

body: Asked our driver to take us there. It was actually a really cheap visit and had really beautiful views of the city. The stature was nice too.
title: Really cool visit

body: nice view Pointmaybe I was having to many places with Buddhas before you can go up in the back, but there is no spectacular view at the end
title: nice view point

body: We loved visiting this temple, and it seemed to not be too popular with tourists so it was lovely and quiet. Stunning statue which you can walk up, and lovely views over the whole of Kandy.
title: Stunning Buddha and beautiful view over Kandy

body: You can climb up the side of the Buddha and get good views of Kandy on a clear day. Not much else around though
title: Great views of Kandy from top of Buddha

body: Maybe the timing was just right, but when we visited we were one of just a few tourist couples there, and were able to sit and enjoy the sweeping view of Kandy from the top of the temple. No entrance fee. Just a donation asked for keeping your shoes safe while you walk around inside. The Buddha is so so, better viewed from afar than up close, but the view of Kandy is second to none. This may be the best kept secret in town.
title: Fantastic view, well kept secret

body: Nothing exclusive to be done here. Statue looks amazing and the only thing you would want to see. Walk around leisurely and do not give into any forced donations!
title: Just the statue

body: Set atop a large hill with splendid views of Kandy city and surrounds, this Buddha statue is a real highlight of Kandy. Climb the staircase behind Buddha for excellent shots and a cool wind to refresh you. As always, keep an eye out for Vishnu. You'll find him somewhere. Inside the Buddha is a little antechamber filled with carvings and splendid tiles, very pretty. Also check out the good bho tree stage.
title: Great views of Kandy, charming temple

body: Pity they don't let you go all the way up and the view is partially blocked at the top. Only from midway can you really enjoy a good view and breeze!
title: Breezy and good view from top!

body: We took a 5 minute tuk tuk ride from Kandy centre for 150 rupees, climbing the steep roads to get there. On arrival you are ordered to leave your fips slops, shoes at a very small stall where they sell coconut and snacks....they do demand a donation...on arrival up the stairs, you are met by a monk who will issue you a ticket for 200 rupees to enter, who then goes and flies his kite in between dealing with tourists.The buddha statue itself is pretty impressive if viewed from far away, like Kandy city, up close and personal it gives a different feeling.We were pretty disappointed only to see the statue with lots of building work going on around, something they didnt tell us at the tourist info office.There is no one at the statue to ask any questions, you are left to walk around at your own leisure.We stayed 5 mins to enjoy the views then left.RecommendationIf you have time, go but tell the tuk tuk driver to wait for you as you wont be long.
title: Great to see from far away

body: one of the best view points to view the whole kandy city. you can travel there by foot or with a vehicle.
title: a view point

body: Very impressive statue and has amazing views of Kandy.Reasonably priced entrance and a couple of contribution boxes.Just respect the place.
title: Big Buddha

body: Dirty and unkept site. Nice lookout. But you don't really have to pay and go in. Could just see from below. Although I saw a chameleon in the garden which was very exciting. Pay 20 rupees for your shoes or just put them in your backpack. They should open a cafe up there....and clean it up.
title: Good view from the top. Meh.

body: It is possible to take a tuk tuk up or make the steep walk to the top wich will take less then 30 minutes from the Tourist Information office near the local bus stand. The views over Kandy and the surrounding hills are certainly worth it.
title: Steep climb to the top, scenic views to be had

body: Bit cheesy unless you are keen on templesNot very oldNot very excitingEasy to access by tuk tuk or cab right to the foot of the statue and not many steps to the top
title: O K

body: The statue is beautiful from far and close. Nothing much to do up there but would recommend to go because of the panoramic view of Kandy.
title: Great Panoramic View of Kandy

body: Left my hostel at quarter to 6 and had a brisk 20 min walk to the top , I'd say from the main road intersection it's about 10/15 mins. It's quite a steep road though but great to walk up nice felling once at the top.Once there I could see a sign instructing you to remove shoes, I put them in my bag and continued. Usually you have to pay but it was early and I had the whole place to myself not one soul, apart from 3 very freindly ( obviously Buddhist) dogs. I put some money in the donation box at the top.Great place to see the sun rise as the Buddha faces east over the river.Excellent experience , I would recommend get up early and take the walk :-) :-) !!
title: Peaceful sunrise spot with a good view

body: This was probably one of the largest Buddha statues I have seen. It has a temple at its base and area to climb a few stories from the back side where you get a view of the city... it also had a nice atmosphere!
title: Impressive statue with a good view

body: This Buddha statute was a good trip and worth the tuktuk ride. You see the Buddha coming into the city and it is it's impressive when you arrive. Beware of the guys collecting echoes at the entrance. 20 Rupee a pair is the norm and the monk is inside collecting the 200 rupee entrance fee. We made the mistake of paying the shoe guys and the monk had to tell us to get our money back. In any case, you can climb up the head of the Buddha if it is open, making it a unique stop and a spectacular view of Kandy Lake.
title: Great View and impressive height

body: We only had a day in Kandy and decided to visit this statue. We took a tuktuk from the tooth temple (1000 rupees there and back).It was lovely to visit this statue. It was quite refreshing that it was not too crowded even on a Saturday afternoon. It was 200 rupees per person to enter which is very affordable. Although this was the only official charge to enter, we were asked to make a donation.The view from the top of the statue is beautiful.
title: Beautiful view from the statue

body: Amazing and imposing statue of Lord Buddha, however approach to the temple needs improvement, overall a good experience and merits a visit
title: Imposing statue of Lord Buddha

body: One of the highlights of my Kandy trip, the white statue of Buddha is imposing and is gorgeous. Must-visit!
title: Gorgeous Buddha in Seated Position

body: You can see the whole kandy city from the top. Great view. What we all liked about the place was that this place was very quite, and relaxing. If you wanna take a break and clear your mind you should definitely visited this place.
title: nice view

body: This is a shrine having an 88 feet Buddha in the samadhi posture. Situated on top of a small hillock, the stairs behind the great statue offer beautiful views. The bodhi tree in the compound is supposed to be grafted from the Great Boddhi tree in India where The Buddha attained enlightenment.
title: See if you have time

body: We were lucky enough to get a blessing from a monk and enjoyed a cup of tea with him. The views from here are amazing.
title: Beautiful Views.

body: Located on a small hill the buddha statue offers also a nice view of the town of Kandy.It's a 30 minutes walk or a short Tuk Tuk drive. Mostly the driver will wait and drive you back to town.Be aware to bring propper clothes to cover shoulders and knees to enter.Admission was around 200-300 LKR.
title: Nice view of the town

body: You can climb up the buddha statue and get the most amazing views. Not too growded and too expensive. Definitely best part of kandy.
title: Beautiful, peaceful

body: the travel was quite exiting as the road is narrow, feel the cold air breezing and such an amazing view specially at the evening!
title: beautiful view!

body: This statue is situated at a nearby hill within the town of Kandy. One can spend a very quiet and pleasant time there. Also, this place gives a nice view of the city.
title: Pleasant and quiet experience

body: We visited the giant white buddha statue, which was large and beautiful. There wasn't much to see in terms a temple there, but you do need to take off your shoes, pay a small fee (200 lkr), and climb 20-30 steps to reach the base. FromThere, you can climb a few more stories to get almost to the top. The very top was closed when we went on dec 20. Would recommend to take a tuk tuk up and back down from the city, as that was part of the experience. The views of kandy were the best part to me!
title: The best thing is the views

body: This is an 88 foot high white meditating Buddha statue situated at the top of a steep hill. There are many bends on the way but you can park at the top. There is a set of about 20 steep steps to get to the base of the statue, where you can wander about and take in the view. Behind the statue is a small temple with a wonderfully coloured and patterned ceiling and plaster images of Buddha's life on the walls. There are a series of metal steps behind the statue which lead to different viewing levels of the panoramic landscape.
title: It's big!

body: Having travelled around Asia numerous times I've seen my fair share of temples and Buddha statues, some of them enormously impressive. The White Buddha, as this one is also called, wasn't one of them unfortunately. It's a twenty minute walk up a hill from Kandy Centre to get there and Rs200 to get in. If you're a fan of these things go to Myanmar next time. The Shwedagon pagoda in Yangon in particular. There's nothing quite like it. A once-in-a-lifetime experience.
title: Not really worth it...

body: Quite a serene location. the view from the top is really great.It is quite clean. however, the administrative staff can pester a bit for donation..
title: Relaxing, good views of kandy town from the top

body: we walked up to the buddha really just to kill time in kandy , otherwise you should really get a tuk tuk,on the arrival the area like most of kandy is really quite filthy , not the buddha itself but the entrance and walk up the buddha itself
title: poor state

body: Unfortunately the stairs all the way to the top weren't open but got some great views of Kandy all the same. Statue looks and feels relatively new, wasn't busy at all, we were the only people there apart from some stray dogs! We got a tuk tuk up there for about 1000 rupee return (about five pounds) from the Temple of the Tooth, flying around the back streets in that was just as fun
title: Great views, but didn't get to the top

body: If you are planning to visit this place I recommend you to go in the night times. You would be able to see the lights of the whole beautiful Kandy city with the beautiful view of Dalanda Maligawa.
title: Go in the Night

body: For me after the temple of the tooth this is a monument number two in Kandy. You can have a nice steep walk up the hill to deserve to see the beautiful view over the Kandy city. Once you get there you can even climb higher on the statue of Buddha and experience even greater 360 degrees outlook and see the green mountains on the horizont. It is absolutely fabulous.Other than that there isnt much to do up there however the short hike especially in hot weather is mentally purgative :-) So dont take a tuk tuk but walk!
title: great view over Kandy

body: The hill the Buddha sits on is a little steep but easy enough to walk up in 10 -15 mins. Shoulders and knees must be covered shoes removed. There is a guy at the bottom who will look after your shoes for a price, we put ours in our bag , costs 200 Rupees per person to go up . A beautiful view from the top. Worth a visit. Follow our journey on Instagram @twolostllamas
title: Great view from the top

body: it is just like the other Buddha Statue, serene and amazing. as a Buddist, it was calming, but some of the other members in the group were bored. If you have seen one, its almost like you have seen it all
title: serene

body: We could see this Buddha from our hotel room so naturally wanted to see it up close and wow!! its easy to get to from anywhere in Kandy - just walk towards it. And I would definitely recommend climbing in the evening after sunset. The Buddha looks amazing when it's lit up and there was no one around! There was just a few people working in some tourist shops, a group of local teens, and the monks. The only tourists we saw was a couple and that was on the way down. The road up to it is a little steep but in no way a trek and not that long a walk considering we walk from our hotel at the other side of the city.
title: Amazing view!!

body: It is worth a visit to this big buddha statue. It is an enormous creature and and is a very powerful place. You can walk up the statue and it delivers a stunning view over Kandy.
title: Big buddha and a beautiful view over the town

body: This beautiful large Buddha overlooks the town of Kandy. To get there, walk to the top of the hill, or take a TukTuk. Once at the top, you enter into the temple area and pay a small fee of $1.35 pp. On the main level, there is a Buddhist gift shop which sells Monk Bags and many other items. A monk is stationed here to give a monks blessing and ties a white string to your wrist while changing. The bracelet remains tied to your wrist till it falls off. On the top Level, after about 3 flights of stairs, there is a platform area with a fabulous views of Kandy. There is a meditation area and a small Buddha hall.
title: Amazing views from the top level.
Bahiravokanda Vihara Buddha Statue
body: Bahiravokanda Vihara Buddha Statue is a must visit place. But I do not recommend on poya (Full Moon) days.

title: The view
body: If you're panorama view lover, that's the place for you in Kandy. Chance to escape from the busy town and see it from peaceful place in other perspective. 200 LR entrance fee + cca 100 LR donation asked.

title: Good walk for a good view...
body: The walk up was good to do after a a fair bit of travelling, not super challenging but nice a sweaty though. You have to leave your shoes and they ask for a donation that you don't have to pay... another 3 metres they bring out the foreigners ticket book for 200 Rupeess.... the view and the breeze worth the effort... big well painted statue is OK if your into that sort of thing too.... Probably do it on the same afternoon you arrive in Kandy and leave the next day after Lake and the temple of the tooth etc...

title: I expect you have travelled a little...
body: And I expect that if you are travelling Sri Lanka you may likely have travelled Thailand. Just assuming here, but follow me on this one.Thailand would make a big deal abiut such a huge hilltop Buddha. They would no doubt have signs. Probably couldn't miss it if you wanted to. It would also have a grand staircase approach. Painted a matching white. It would be free and busy with locals.Not the case here in Kandy. If you don't take the correct road, you will be like every other tourist, caught in the double helix of roads that circumnavigate the hillside, so close but so far from the smugly smiling Buddha above.If you do make it up, you will be asked for a shoe minding donation, then 200 rupees entry fee. What do you get for that? A nice view.

title: Its ok
body: the buddha statue was not the best that we have seen, and considering the walk to get here we were hoping for better. the statues was covered in scaffolding. Appreciate that the statue needs to be maintained but we still paid full price to see it, slightly disappointed!

title: Incredible view of Kandy during sunset, very neat statue
body: from the lake it takes a little over 10 minutes to get to the statue and the tuk tuk ride cost us about 300 rupee since it was up the hill. Really great view at sunset, absolutely worth going to if you have a free night in Kandy.

title: Foreigners have to pay!!
body: The walk up is very steep but rewarding when we got here you have to take your shoes off which is the norm but again a "donation" was needed for it and when we entered foreigners had to pay 200 each which annoyed me further as I Sri Lankans don't have to pay. But we walked all the way up so went in (at night) and to be fair the view of Kandy where good but the temple itself wasn't that impressive!

title: Imposing statue overlooking city
body: Reminded me very much of a similar statue overlooking Phuket Thailand. Can get busy but worth the visit and the views

title: Buddha Watching Kandy city
body: Couldn't get spare time to visit the place actually but had a nice view of Buddha watching the city from Kandy view point

title: A good monument to add to the beauty of Kandy
body: This monument stands tall in the hills surrounding Kandy. It adds a lot of beauty to the city. But nothing as such to go and visit.
